profile.reading:
This building, VA15, sits on Vantage's Ashburn I campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166, per this registry's address matching; Vantage does not publish an individual facility page or press release for VA15 specifically. Vantage's current campus page describes Ashburn I as 52 acres with six data centers totaling 1.7 million square feet at full buildout and 206 megawatts of critical IT load, a building count matching the VA11 through VA16 numbering tracked in this registry (VA11 at 30MW, VA12 at 32MW, and VA13 at 44MW are individually confirmed via Vantage press releases elsewhere in this registry), though Vantage does not explicitly confirm on its own site that VA15 specifically is one of the six, and no individual sqft or MW figure for VA15 is published anywhere found this session.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility: in November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, per Inside Climate News.

Northern Virginia's Loudoun and Prince William counties together form the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and local zoning debate has intensified as residents, county supervisors, and Dominion Energy weigh the tradeoff between commercial tax revenue and rising transmission-line construction, land consumption, and residential electricity-rate pressure tied to data center growth. Dominion Energy's long-range integrated resource plans have repeatedly cited this region's data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's near-term generation and transmission capital spending, a dynamic that has drawn scrutiny from the Virginia State Corporation Commission in periodic rate cases. As documented in this profile's address and campus fields, this building's assignment to the Vantage campus it is grouped under is inferred from building-count and geographic proximity matching against Vantage's own published campus materials rather than from a Vantage-confirmed individual building name, so it should be read as a reasonable but unconfirmed placement pending direct operator confirmation.

reading.body:
Vantage Data Centers operates the Ashburn I campus in Sterling, Virginia as six multi-story facilities identified as VA11 through VA16. The operator publishes 206 MW of critical IT load and 1.7 million square feet across the full campus at buildout, with over 1 million square feet already operational. No individual building figure for VA15 specifically has been published. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, the 206 MW campus total represents roughly 5,150 racks of potential AI capacity. The campus sits at densities up to 300 watts per square foot, which places it at the upper end of current data center engineering practice for colocation operations.

This campus ranks 24th among Virginia facilities with published megawatt figures. The state context shows 326 total mapped facilities in Virginia but only 23 with published power specifications from operator pages, of which this campus represents roughly 15 percent of the state's total published capacity of 1,375 MW. The concentration of Virginia's published capacity in a small set of facilities means that Ashburn I is material to the state's grid footprint.

The operator's published specifications do not detail which power utilities serve the site, what the interconnection timeline is, or what portion of the 206 MW is already drawing power versus allocated to future buildout. The certifications for this campus and whether it qualifies for any specific workload class are not published. Whether Ashburn I has secured power supply commitments or faces grid constraints that would affect the timeline to activation is not stated in the operator's public materials.
